name: HEDISCoreEncounter
title: HEDIS Core Encounter
description: The HEDIS Core Encounter profile extends the US Core requirements to include requirements for measure calculation.

element.definition: [HEDIS] The metadata about a resource. This is content in the resource that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.
[US Core] Identifier(s) by which this encounter is known.
[US Core] Establishes the namespace for the value - that is, a URL that describes a set values that are unique.
[US Core] The portion of the identifier typically relevant to the user and which is unique within the context of the system.
[US Core] planned | arrived | triaged | in-progress | onleave | finished | cancelled +.
[US Core] Concepts representing classification of patient encounter such as ambulatory (outpatient), inpatient, emergency, home health or others due to local variations.
[US Core] Specific type of encounter (e.g. e-mail consultation, surgical day-care, skilled nursing, rehabilitation).

element.short: The patient present at the encounter
element.definition: [HEDIS] The patient present at the encounter.
[US Core] The list of people responsible for providing the service.
[US Core] Role of participant in encounter.
[US Core] The period of time that the specified participant participated in the encounter. These can overlap or be sub-sets of the overall encounter's period.
[HEDIS][US Core] Persons involved in the encounter other than the patient.
[HEDIS][US Core] The start and end time of the encounter.
element.comment: Period of the encounter is a critical factor for most HEDIS measures and cannot be omitted.

element.definition: [US Core] Reason the encounter takes place, expressed as a code. For admissions, this can be used for a coded admission diagnosis.
[HEDIS] The list of diagnosis relevant to this encounter.

[HEDIS] Reason the encounter takes place, as specified using information from another resource. For admissions, this is the admission diagnosis. The indication will typically be a Condition (with other resources referenced in the evidence.detail), or a Procedure.
[US Core] Details about the admission to a healthcare service.
[US Core] Category or kind of location after discharge.
[US Core] List of locations where  the patient has been during this encounter.
[US Core] The location where the encounter takes place.
